checked.why:
I read the finding by its own id, the first of seven in audit/findings-1.2.118/domain-map-b-movement.json, and followed the whole road on b5a29e73's code without running anything. The Spectator's own browser treats the move as a ghost's and records nothing. On the primary GM, though, the updateToken hook noteGmPosition calls judgeArrival for this token, and nothing on that road leaves a Spectator out.

The steps on the primary, in order:
- The actor is type "character" and the mover is a player, so the judge runs.
- crossingVerdict returns true for the spectator flag, and that makes `counted` true.
- eclipseSighting gates only a Monokuma and crossesFree, which is a Monocub only. A Spectator is not a Monocub, so its crossing is counted.
- noteCrossing gates only a Monokuma, so the crossing is written to crossingStore.
- recordCrossingInStep calls scheduleSettle, and two seconds later settle fires drpgCrossingSettled.
- onWatchCrossing whispers `{name} comes into {room}` to the watcher, using the actor's raw `mover.name`. There is no nameAsSeen, no veil and no Spectator check on that line.

auditMove's Spectator exemption (movement-audit.mjs:339-340) runs after the judge, so it cannot undo the counted sighting or the recorded crossing.

A kept death makes this actor at the kill (death.mjs:203, ensureDeadSpectator kept:true). The actor gets the student's name (spectator-dead.mjs Actor.create name: student.name), the spectator flag and no link flag, and its token is placed where the body lies.

What already exists in tests and decisions:
- No test drives a Spectator's move on the primary and checks crossingStore, the Eclipse count or the watch. My grep of the tier files and of 21-masked-killer found none.
- No decision in docs/dev/e112, e112v, owner-115 or owner-116 accepts this. A grep for e118 found nothing.
- The nearest recorded acceptance is Q-C3b-1 in spectator-dead.mjs's header: the owner accepted that "a console can read the death off" the watcher actor's world data. That covers a console reading world data. It does not cover the module itself putting a card in a classmate's chat.
- A sibling finding (domain-item-b-gm-panel) covers a different road, namesIn at the watch's start.

Severity stays major, not blocker. The card does not name the killer, and "Aiko comes into Library" reads the same as a living Aiko walking, so it does not reveal the death on its face. It does give the watcher a false sighting of the victim after the death: a wrong Eclipse alibi and a wrong timeline in an ordinary case, and a wrong entry in the watch's end-of-Eclipse summary. That breaks the Keep Watch rule and the investigation in a normal situation. A living Spectator's walk (the role, not a death) is reported the same way; that is wrong but no secret.

What I could not settle by reading: that a real Foundry lets the victim's player drag the watcher token during a Night Eclipse with nothing else stopping it.

checked.failure_scenario: During a Night Eclipse a student is killed and the GMs keep the death. Her player walks her Spectator, named after her, into the Library that a classmate keeps watch over. The primary GM counts and records the crossing as a student's, and the classmate's whisper reads "Aiko comes into Library." - a false sighting of the victim after her death, which also goes into the watch's summary at the Eclipse's end.

checked.why: The finding was read under its own id, domain-map-c-rooms-1. I traced the road from the sheet's Give button to the option text, and no guard on it reads the veil. Press: sheet-inventory.mjs addHandoverButton checks only rowGate (the sheet's mode), then calls handOverDialog -> askRecipient -> askWhoIsHere. The phase gate there is allowedNow's "handover" road, which shuts only for an Eclipse, so the victim and bystanders can open it while the opening waits. The list is othersInRoom -> othersInNamedRoom -> countsAsPresent. That predicate leaves out Monokuma, a Spectator, the dead and a token the GM hid (hiddenByGm reads `hidden` alone). Since E112v the veil writes no `hidden`, so the veiled killer counts as present on every browser. roomOfToken reads the document's x and y, not the module's display verdict, so the killer is placed in the room. Each option is drawn with nameAsSeen, which hides a name only for a masked actor (isMaskedActor reads the `masked` flag). The veil sets `veiled`, and the mask goes on only after a successful opening, so during the veil the real name is printed. tokenShownTo hides the token on that same browser ("hide" for anyone who is not the owner or on the killers' side). The one road where the victim's screen never showed the killer is a murder declared in an Eclipse: every token is dark until the veil takes over at the lights, so the picker is the first thing that names the killer there. The GM's transferRefusal runs only after the list is drawn. No test pins the opposite and no decision records it as accepted. R7404 and scenario 21's picker checks cover the mask ("?") only, and the scenario's veil checks read tokenShownTo, the canvas and the ruler, never a picker. The one recorded known leak, foundry-veiled-token-actor, is about a console reading the flag, not a normal UI window. E112's decision that the veiled killer stays "in the room" (STATUS.md, R7705) covers counting them, not naming them. The owner's rule as written in mask-gm.mjs says the killer is hidden "from every player but the killer's side, bystanders included". Severity: 11.3 puts "zdradza odpowiedz" (gives the answer away) at blocker, and this names a hidden killer to the victim and bystanders through an ordinary button. The finder's "major" undercounts it. One limit: this is a static read only, nothing was run.
